title: Systematic overlap between dropped enforcement and Trump donors
summary: The overlap is documented. The NYT (Dec 14, 2025, known only secondhand here) found the SEC eased about 60% of the crypto cases it inherited (reportedly 14 of 23), against roughly 4% for other cases, with Trump-tied firms common among them. Robinhood gave $2M to the inauguration and had its SEC crypto probe closed. Public Citizen counts hundreds of halted corporate actions, 23 of them crypto. Gemini gave 1.5M USDC to MAGA Inc. Causation is not shown: firms with no known Trump donations (Uniswap, OpenSea, Yuga, Immutable) got the same treatment, the NYT found no evidence of direct pressure, and the SEC and Atkins deny political influence. The fee for Crypto.com's Trump-linked lobbyist (Jeff Miller) is unconfirmed.

sub_claims.statement: A New York Times analysis found the SEC eased about 60% of the crypto cases it inherited, several of them tied to Trump donors or business partners.
sub_claims.finding: Multiple outlets report the NYT analysis (published about Dec 14, 2025). It found the SEC dismissed, paused or cut penalties in more than 60% of the crypto cases active on Jan 20, 2025, reportedly 14 of 23, against about 4% of inherited non-crypto cases, and filed no new crypto cases. Firms with Trump ties (Binance, Ripple, Justin Sun/Tron, the Winklevoss-backed Gemini) are among the eased cases. Secondhand accounts disagree on how many of the 14 had Trump ties: 'eight' in one, 'all' in another. That breakdown is unverified because the original was not reachable. The NYT found no evidence that Trump directly pressured the SEC.

sub_claims.statement: Robinhood, an inaugural donor, had its SEC crypto probe closed.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC Enforcement Division told Robinhood on Feb 21, 2025 that it was closing its Robinhood Crypto investigation with no action. That probe had produced a Wells notice in May 2024. Robinhood announced the closure on Feb 24, 2025. Robinhood gave $2M to the Trump-Vance Inaugural Committee, per filings reported by Bloomberg and InvestmentNews. Timing aside, no link between the two is documented, and the closure came in the same week as the Coinbase, Uniswap and OpenSea closures.

sub_claims.statement: Public Citizen tracks halted corporate enforcement actions against companies with Trump ties.
sub_claims.finding: Public Citizen's Corporate Enforcement Tracker counted 109 thwarted actions in early 2025 and 159 canceled or halted actions against 166 corporations by the end of year one. Its September 2026 update says inherited actions against 205 corporations were canceled. Its 'Deleting Tech Enforcement' report found that 23 of the dropped or halted tech actions involved crypto firms (20 withdrawn, 3 halted). It links them to about $1.2B in tech-sector political influence spending, including Coinbase ($76.1M) and Ripple ($55M). Public Citizen is an advocacy group, and its counts mix investigations with cases. Its own statement that 'firms close to Trump benefit' is framing rather than a measured correlation.

AP (Dec 2025) reports that from late 2024 Crypto.com increased its lobbying payments to Jeff Miller of Miller Strategies, a GOP fundraiser and finance chair of Trump's inaugural festivities. Per the disclosures, he lobbied the White House and the SEC. AP also reports that Biden-era commissioners had authorized charges and that Crypto.com negotiated to delay any filing until after the inauguration. Crypto.com says Miller 'had no involvement' with the SEC investigation, and Miller did not comment. The fee amounts paid to Miller were not found, so they are unverified. Crypto.com's parent reported $500K of in-house lobbying in Q3 2025.

An FEC filing reported in early January 2026 shows Gemini Trust Company gave 1.5M USDC to MAGA Inc., liquidated on receipt, alongside two $10M gifts from Crypto.com's parent Foris DAX. MAGA Inc.'s July 2026 report then showed the Winklevoss twins giving two contributions of more than $5M each in BTC on June 19, 2026. Those came about three weeks after the CFTC joined Gemini's May 27-28, 2026 motion to vacate its $5M 2025 consent judgment. Judge Hellerstein (SDNY) denied that motion in Oct 2026, a ruling found in one report only. No link between the gifts and the CFTC's move is documented.

sub_claims.statement: Counter-argument: the policy shift also covered firms with no Trump ties.
sub_claims.finding: The SEC closed probes into Uniswap Labs (Feb 25, 2025), OpenSea (Feb 21), Yuga Labs (Mar 3) and Immutable (Mar 25) with no action. None of these firms is a known Trump donor. The SEC said its Crypto Task Force under Peirce was reassessing how securities law applies to digital assets. The near-total crypto retreat suggests a sector-wide policy change, not a donor-specific one. Still, the NYT's crypto-versus-non-crypto gap (about 60% vs 4%) and the many donors among the beneficiaries are why critics see favoritism.

The SEC told the NYT that politics played no role and that its decisions were legal and policy calls. At a Feb 11, 2026 House Financial Services hearing, Atkins answered 'no' when Rep. Sylvia Garcia asked whether Trump, his family, cabinet or White House staff had ever asked him to take or decline an enforcement action. He added 'we are bringing cases' and would not speak to the Trump family's business. Reps. Waters, Casten and Sherman wrote on Jan 15, 2026 that the dismissals create 'the unmistakable inference of a pay-to-play scheme.' Peirce said there is 'not a pass on securities violations.' The White House (Leavitt) says neither the President nor his family engage in conflicts of interest.

sub_claims.statement: The overlap is systematic evidence of pay-to-play.
sub_claims.finding: No document, testimony or official finding shows a donation or deal was exchanged for an enforcement outcome. The case rests on correlation and timing, the crypto-versus-non-crypto disparity and the prominence of donors. All of it is consistent with favoritism but also with a sector-wide deregulatory policy.

corrections: The 'about 60%' NYT figure covers cases dismissed, paused or given reduced penalties (eased), not only cases dropped. Secondhand accounts disagree on how many of those cases had Trump ties.
Gemini's 1.5M USDC MAGA Inc. gift came from Gemini Trust Company. The larger June 2026 BTC gifts (>$5M each) came from Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss personally, made via Gemini.
Crypto.com runs mostly in-house lobbying. Its link to Jeff Miller is reported by AP, but the fee amounts were not confirmed.
denials_and_context: The SEC told the NYT that political favoritism played no role. Atkins testified that no one in Trump's circle asked him to take or decline an enforcement action.
Crypto.com says its SEC probe closed for lack of merit, with 'absolutely no connection' to its political activity, and that Miller had no involvement.
Robinhood's chief legal and compliance officer, Dan Gallagher, said the probe 'never should have been opened.'

Non-donor firms (Uniswap, OpenSea, Yuga Labs, Immutable) also had probes closed, which supports the policy-shift explanation. The SEC still settled some matters with payments, e.g. Rainberry's $10M in the Justin Sun case (Mar 2026), and Ripple's $125M judgment stands.

Public Citizen and House Democrats are partisan or advocacy sources. Their 'pay-to-play' framing is an inference, and Public Citizen notes that inclusion in its tracker does not mean proven misconduct.
